texts: Dwellings per year by component (top row: unexplained building, thousand per year)
Negative part: outline in its colour, hanging from the top of the stack
Net replacement, history (census dwelling counts; parts not separable)
Net total of a bar with a negative part
Reference, history: census empty / private dwellings (before 2013: unoccupied × the 2013 empty share), linear between censuses
Reference, projection: held at the 2023 census value (5.39%)
Reference, projection: implied by the held rate + the unabsorbed 2026 overbuild / stock
Sensitivity, not used by the Reference: one definition, pooled 2018/2023 empty share
note: a: The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the 2026 overbuild raises implied stock vacancy temporarily and is absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). c: the unconsented additions each vacancy definition requires to close the stock identity (BRANZ demolition rate); counting residents-away dwellings as vacant requires implausibly many. b: History: one bar per census interval (interval means; vacancy on one definition, the pooled 2018/2023 empty share, 49.2% of unoccupied dwellings); between censuses annual detail is not identified. Faint bar: 2024–2025, households consent-derived. Projection annual, lighter. History: net replacement is census-measured, the rate of the census dwelling-count identity of each interval (SF3; under-construction corrected) x the previous year's stock, the quantity the model uses (2024–2025: the latest rate carried). Projection: demolition replacement, unconsented additions (negative), the recent replacement surge, retirement villages (negative), the 2026 overbuild and the overbuild absorbed (negative payback). Negative parts are outlined, hanging from the top of the positive stack; each bar ends at its net total (tick). Unexplained building (faded red; its value per interval in the row at the top, thousand dwellings per year): building not explained by household formation, vacancy and census-measured replacement: redevelopment not captured by the census counts, error in the household estimates, or residual; it may be negative.
